\begin{defn}[Directed graph]
A \emph{directed graph} $G = \tuple{V, E}$ is a set of
\emph{vertices}~$V$ and a set of \emph{edges}~$E \subseteq V^2$.
\end{defn}

\begin{explain}
According to our definition, a graph just is a set together with a
relation on that set.  Of course, when talking about graphs, it's only
natural to expect that they are graphically represented: we can draw a
graph by connecting two vertices~$v_1$ and $v_2$ by an arrow iff
$\tuple{v_1, v_2} \in E$.  The only difference between a relation by
itself and a graph is that a graph specifies the set of vertices,
i.e., a graph may have isolated vertices. The important point,
however, is that every relation~$R$ on a set~$X$ can be seen as a
directed graph $\tuple{X, R}$, and conversely, a directed
graph~$\tuple{V, E}$ can be seen as a relation $E \subseteq V^2$ with
the set $V$ explicitly specified.
\end{explain}

\begin{prop}
Suppose $R \subseteq A \times B$ has the property that whenever $Rxy$
and $Rxy'$ then $y = y'$.  Then $R$ is the graph of the partial
function $f\colon A \pto B$ defined by: if there is a $y$ such that
$Rxy$, then $f(x) = y$, otherwise $f(x) \fundefined$.  If $R$ is also
\emph{serial}, i.e., for each $x \in A$ there is a $y \in B$ such that
$Rxy$, then $f$ is total.
\end{prop}

\begin{proof}
Suppose there is a $y$ such that $Rxy$.  If there were another $y'
\neq y$ such that $Rxy'$, the condition on $R$ would be
violated. Hence, if there is a $y$ such that $Rxy$, that $y$ is
unique, and so $f$ is well-defined.  Obviously, $R_f = R$ and $f$ is
total if~$R$ is serial.
\end{proof}

prepared_changes_preserved.sense: A mathematical set is a collection treated as one object, determined by its members rather than their order or repetition. This noun can denote sets of worlds, formulas, numbers, functions or other objects; it is distinct from the English verb 'set', such as 'set up'.
prepared_changes_preserved.rationale: New independent assessment (2026-09-06): Retain مجموعة because the primary definition explicitly introduces membership, the empty set and extensionality, while the inspected later contexts use the noun across different kinds of members. Those local definitions do not prove the retained rationale's claim of universal cross-regional standardness. Nor does a bare set name imply the added operation and laws of an algebraic group, so زمرة should not be substituted indiscriminately. Inspection of all 37 retained English/MSA locator pairs found one genuine verb/noun mismatch (OLP-0609: set up) and two same-noun but different-passage bindings (OLP-0023 and OLP-0332). These are rejected locator claims, not accusations that the Arabic word مجموعة is mistranslated. Exact replacement witnesses are supplied; the original recorded fields are preserved. This assessment is provisional and open to correction; no original translator deliberation or official dictionary attestation is claimed.

changes.sense: For a surjection f:A→B, a right inverse h:B→A chooses one preimage per y∈B and satisfies f(h(y))=y. Axiom of Choice supports the general simultaneous-selection assertion, while particular cases can be proved without it.
changes.rationale: New independent assessment (2026-09-06): Retain معكوس أيمن for f∘h=id_B and بديهية الاختيار for the general principle named in the footnote. Nonempty fibres alone do not specify a global selection. The exceptions matter: a natural-number domain supplies least preimages, a finite domain can be finitely ordered, and a bijection has unique preimages. The passage therefore does not claim that every particular inverse construction requires the axiom. The retained longer headword is explanatory; the two literal labels occur separately. Right follows the composition identity, not visual placement in RTL. This assessment is provisional and open to correction, not a reconstruction of the original translator's deliberation or an official dictionary attestation. Independent admission readback (2026-09-06): The displayed equation fixes right inverse independently of physical RTL placement. The footnote explicitly exempts finite, natural-number and bijective cases; least or unique preimages explain those exceptions without silently strengthening the general choice-free assertion.
